tips.title: Define virtual tool in XML format
tips.body: Create a .vtx file with an ID matching the macro database and place it in the same location.

tips.title: Set tool data mode to VT
tips.body: In hyperMILL, set the Tool Data Mode to 'VT' and use the ID of the virtual tool.

tips.title: Use RuleFilter for tool selection
tips.body: Define multiple RuleFilters within SearchFilters to combine conditions with 'And' logic.

tips.title: Set user variable in PreSearchActions
tips.body: Use <Action Type='SetUserVariable'> to define variables before tool search.

tips.title: Define post search actions for ToolFound and ToolNotFound
tips.body: Use <ToolFound> and <ToolNotFound> to define actions based on whether a tool is found or not.

tips.title: Define select priority for virtual tools
tips.body: Set global or local select priorities using <SelectPriority> with multiple <SelectStrategy> elements.

tips.title: Supported select strategies
tips.body: Four strategies: Min, Max, Sequence, Condition.

tips.title: Variable format in virtual tool definition
tips.body: Variables use the format Object.Parameter or Object.SubObject::Parameter.

tips.title: Commonly used tool variables
tips.body: List of commonly used parameters like NCTool.UsableLength, MillingTool.Diameter.

tips.title: MacroTool variables
tips.body: Supported parameters include ID, NCNumber, Diameter, CornerRadius.

tips.title: Feature variables
tips.body: Combine main parameters with base object parameters using :: separator.

tips.title: Connector variables
tips.body: Return parameters of current active feature connection item, e.g., Connector.Diameter.

tips.title: JobCfg variables
tips.body: Can be used as variables, e.g., JobCfg.*Comment.

tips.title: Joblist variables
tips.body: Select machine and material in joblist, e.g., Joblist.Machine.

tips.title: Macro variables
tips.body: Define machine and material groups in macro, e.g., Macro.MachineGroup.

tips.title: Window system environment variables
tips.body: Return values of window system environment variables, e.g., EnvVariable.USERNAME.
